analysis.title: GS MarketStrats: After the Common Shock (Vitali Meschoulam, 9 Nov 2026)
key_insights: The framework has moved from reflation versus constraint to constraint versus transmission. Real yields rose and imposed a higher cost of capital. 10y real yields are at about 2.50% to 2.60%.
GS expects exhaustion of the rates sell-off into year-end, not yet a secular duration rally. For 2027 the opportunity lies in markets where the pause becomes a policy turn.

The Democratic midterm sweep reduced two premia: the AI infrastructure premium in equities and the Iran conflict and inflation premium in oil and bonds. Gridlock is not fiscal repair, and the US deficit is still expected to stay near 6% of GDP.

Brent fell about 9% on 4 Nov after the election, extending a de-escalation repricing already underway. GS calls this a change in probabilities, not a resolution, and notes Gulf refining capacity would not be repaired immediately.

The equity correction is concentrated in sectors exposed to AI scrutiny and geopolitical de-escalation, so GS reads it as political and sector-specific rather than macroeconomic. It is the first test of the transmission thesis.

GS sees the AI theme as repriced, not invalidated. Cash-generative hyperscalers can sustain investment, while marginal infrastructure projects must clear a much higher real hurdle rate. Companies capturing AI productivity gains without financing the buildout may offer cleaner upside.

Since early Nov, 10y yields fell about 7bp in the US, 15bp in the UK, 7bp in Germany, 10bp in Japan, 13bp in Australia and 14bp in Canada. After a year in which 27 of 30 tracked countries saw higher 10y yields, this extends a 30-45bp retracement that signals stabilisation, not yet a peak.

The pause in the sell-off becomes durable only if four conditions hold: de-escalation persists in oil, the equity correction moderates AI infrastructure spending, lower inflation comes with slower nominal demand, and investors absorb heavy sovereign and corporate issuance without a higher term premium.

Nominal growth is the hinge. Resilient growth keeps real yields elevated. A gradual slowdown lets duration rally and central banks eventually turn. An abrupt slowdown produces a bigger bond rally but widens credit spreads, weakens equities and restores dollar safe-haven demand.

The curve splits into policy-sensitive and supply-sensitive duration. With 2y US yields above 4.5%, investors need more compensation to hold long-dated sovereign and corporate supply. Intermediate maturities can perform once markets stop adding hikes. Long ends stay constrained by issuance and term premium.

Regional duration views: US prefer the belly to the long end. Euro area prefer policy-sensitive core duration. UK is a conditional duration trade needing wage and services inflation confirmation. Japan stays outside the broad duration position.

EM views are framework-derived and dispersed: Poland and South Africa offer conditional convexity, Mexico has a clearer policy turn but FX risk, India and Czech Republic are nearer stabilisation than easing, Brazil, Turkey and Hungary are high-carry markets driven by fiscal and currency credibility, and Israel is primarily a political trade.

The thesis fails in one direction if oil rebounds, AI capex reaccelerates and nominal growth ignores high real yields, which would resume the global rates sell-off. It fails in the other direction if nominal growth weakens fast enough for a broad easing cycle, which helps government bonds but hurts equities, credit and EM beta.

sector_views.rationale: Selectively buy where valuations have reset but earnings and strategic investment remain intact. Favour companies monetising AI productivity over marginal infrastructure and financing-dependent beneficiaries.
Marginal projects must clear a much higher real hurdle rate. Strategic capex from cash-generative hyperscalers is distinguished from projects that only worked at lower rates.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Keeps the market on the constraint side of the framework and tightens financial conditions.
High front-end yields offer return without much duration risk, so investors demand more compensation for long-dated supply.
Gridlock does not repair the deficit, so sovereign supply keeps pressure on the long end.
De-escalation repricing lowers inflation pressure and reduces the case for further Fed tightening.

trade_ideas.rationale: US political and geopolitical exceptionalism is fading.

risk_factors: Markets may confuse removal of one inflationary tail with the end of structural capital demand.
Heavy sovereign issuance and AI-related corporate financing could keep real yields elevated and push term premium higher.
Oil could rebound if de-escalation reverses, restoring the inflation premium.
AI capex could reaccelerate with nominal growth insensitive to high real yields, resuming the global rates sell-off.
An abrupt nominal growth slowdown would widen credit spreads, weaken equities and EM beta, and lift the dollar.
Broadening earnings weakness, wider credit spreads and slower hiring would show the rate constraint transmitting to the economy.
geopolitical: Iran risk premium embedded in oil and inflation has moderated after the Democratic midterm sweep and a de-escalation repricing.
A political settlement would not immediately repair Gulf refining capacity or fully reverse the physical energy shock.
Congress may constrain foreign-policy funding and parts of the administration's trade agenda.
Israel is described as primarily a political trade, where a more stable post-election equilibrium would support the shekel, credit and inflation outlook.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil is lower, geopolitical risk has moderated, AI capex is questioned and further central-bank tightening is less likely, so the sell-off is exhausting and intermediate duration can perform.
tension_points.bear_case: Heavy sovereign issuance, AI-related corporate financing and resilient nominal growth keep real yields elevated and long ends constrained by term premium.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil rebounds, AI capex reaccelerates and nominal growth remains insensitive to high real yields, which would resume the global rates sell-off.

tension_points.bull_case: The correction is political and sector-specific, so technology valuations reset without an economy-wide earnings collapse, creating a buying opportunity in parts of tech.
tension_points.bear_case: If earnings weakness broadens, credit spreads widen and hiring slows, the rate constraint is transmitting into the wider economy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Broadening earnings weakness, wider credit spreads and slower hiring would show the constraint transmitting beyond the AI sector.
